meta.name: Job Radar — Regina · Toronto · Alberta
meta.profile_summary: UX/Product designer, 9 yrs (Software QA → UX/UI). Enterprise SaaS, loyalty/financial rules engines, POS/procurement, design systems, Figma + React/HTML/CSS. MSc HCI (University of Regina, thesis: AI-assisted search for students with dyslexia), graduating Dec 2027. Past: VFX rotoscoping lead + instructor, creative strategist/print.

regions.regina: Regina (plus Saskatoon / remote roles held by SK employers)

categories.most_matched: match_score ≥ 78 and role is realistically winnable now or at graduation
categories.urgent_apply: closing ≤ 10 days, a term starting ≤ 2 months (internships), or a fast-moving high-fit role first seen ≤ 3 days ago
categories.student_track: compatible with being a full-time grad student: part-time, casual, flexible contract, co-op/internship, on-campus
categories.ai_frontier: role designs, evaluates or builds AI products. This is the booming segment to grow into
categories.remote_canada: can be done from Regina (remote within Canada)
categories.grad_2027_pipeline: recurring program or cohort type to target for a Dec 2027 / Jan 2028 start
categories.watchlist: strong-fit employer or closed or blocked post; watch for the next opening

meta.scoring: 0–100. +role-family fit (AI product / UX / accessibility / service design highest), +domain overlap (enterprise SaaS, fintech, rules engines, POS, edtech/reading, health), +seniority fit (3–9 yrs), +AI-native tooling asks, +accessibility, +remote-Canada; −engineering-only, −hard eligibility blockers, −junior/print-only.
meta.salary_note: salary_min_cad/max_cad are annual CAD; hourly rates are annualized × 2080 h. salary_text keeps the original wording.
meta.dedupe_rule: Same job = same normalized employer + normalized title + region (or same URL). On a repeat sighting: keep first_seen, set last_seen to today, times_seen += 1, append a history event only when something changed.
meta.size_policy: When this file passes ~1.5 MB or 2,500 jobs, move jobs with status closed/filled/likely_closed and last_seen older than 120 days to data/archive/jobs-<year>.json, and add the path to meta.archives. runs[] keeps daily summaries forever (it is small).

worked: WebSearch across Indeed, Glassdoor, CareerBeacon, Wellfound, Built In, IxDF, ZipRecruiter, ALIS, Alberta job postings, Greenhouse/Lever/Workable ATS pages
blocked_or_thin: Indeed/Glassdoor pages not fetched directly; details from snippets

runs.notes: Seed scan. Many postings come from search snippets, so posting dates are often unknown; first_seen is the radar date.

opportunities.name: Mitacs Accelerate research internship
opportunities.where: Anywhere in Canada (you stay a U of R student)
opportunities.what: A 4-month paid research internship with a company or non-profit, supervised by your professor. Open to international students. Pitch your dyslexia-search/MINDS thesis to an edtech, library-software or accessibility company and do the internship on that project.
opportunities.action: Ask Orland about a Mitacs-eligible partner (library/edtech/a11y vendor). Draft a 1-page project pitch in December.

opportunities.name: AI Career Accelerator Program (AICAP) + Work-Integrated Learning (WILOs)
opportunities.type: career program + paid part-time AI work
opportunities.what: Probably the Alberta AI program you heard about. Amii's flagship pathway for graduate-level AI talent, with coaching, career exploration and paid WILO placements under 20 h/week. It does NOT guarantee a job: Amii says participation doesn't guarantee placement. It targets technical AI master's/PhD students; non-CS grads are considered in limited cases.
opportunities.action: Apply framing your thesis as applied AI (LLM scaffold + HCI evaluation). Email talent@amii.ca first to ask whether an HCI/AI thesis qualifies.

opportunities.name: ML Residency
opportunities.what: Paid early-career roles on real AI projects with an Amii mentor. Engineering-weighted.
opportunities.action: Watch the Amii careers page from fall 2027.

opportunities.name: Upper Bound 2027 (AI conference) + talent bursaries
opportunities.deadline: Event May 18–21, 2027; bursary intake usually opens months ahead
opportunities.what: Canada's largest AI conference (11,000 attendees in 2026). A limited number of talent bursaries go to students and early-career professionals each year, and past bursaries covered travel. Most of Alberta's AI employers are there in one week.
opportunities.action: Apply for a talent bursary as soon as it opens. Submit a poster or demo of MINDS if there's a call.

opportunities.name: National AI Literacy Initiative (free)
opportunities.what: $13M federal program offering free practical AI learning to up to one million post-secondary students. Good for quick badges, but it won't set you apart much.
opportunities.action: Take the courses for badges in an evening or two. Don't spend more time than that.

opportunities.name: Co.Labs: Uniting the Prairies conference + Expert/X-in-Residence program
opportunities.what: Saskatchewan's largest tech event (75+ investors, 150+ startups). Co.Labs also contracts senior specialists, UX/UI among them, to mentor startups one-on-one. That's paid, flexible work that puts you in front of every SK founder.
opportunities.action: Email Co.Labs about the Expert program with your Annex Cloud case study, and attend UTP 2027.

opportunities.name: ComIT AI & Machine Learning Upskilling
opportunities.deadline: Pilot ended Oct 2026; expanded funding Nov 2026
opportunities.what: Three-month AI/ML program with resume, job-search and interview support. Pilot: 21 finished, 11 employed (4 in tech). Only for unemployed or underemployed SK residents, so it's a fallback after graduation.
opportunities.action: Bookmark it for January 2028 if you don't have an offer by then.

opportunities.name: Built Smart AI (Calgary)
opportunities.what: Government-funded no-code AI program with employer connections and job placement support. Only for unemployed or underemployed Albertans, and aimed at construction and related industries. Only relevant if you move to Calgary without an offer.
opportunities.action: Not for now. A fallback only.

opportunities.name: Vector Scholarship in AI
opportunities.what: Entrance award for AI master's students at Ontario universities only, so not available to a U of R student. Listed so you don't spend time on it.

opportunities.name: Provincial tech nominee pathways (relocation factor)
opportunities.what: Alberta's Accelerated Tech Pathway (Express Entry candidates with an Alberta tech job offer, ~600 nominations in 2026). Saskatchewan has a Tech Talent Pathway and a Student category tied to graduating from and working in Saskatchewan. Where you work after graduating can decide which of these you can use.
opportunities.action: Before choosing a city, check which pathway each job offer unlocks (see the sask-pr checklist).

intel.headline: Aim for AI-product UX with an accessibility edge. Target Calgary for the move, Toronto for the AI-design volume, and use Regina as your base until graduation.

focus_roles.role: AI Product Designer / UX for AI experiences
focus_roles.why: About half of the high-fit Toronto and Calgary posts in this scan are AI-product roles, and several explicitly ask for Claude Code, Cursor or v0. AI-skilled workers across the US and Canada grew 45% year over year (CBRE). Your Bookkeeper AI human-in-the-loop prototype and the MINDS LLM scaffold are exactly the evidence they ask for.

Toronto banks, Kobo, YuJa and Fable keep posting accessibility specialist roles (AODA compliance demand). Few designers can claim research on readers with dyslexia, which makes this your differentiator.

Edmonton has 23 Vantix service-designer seats plus 7 permanent GoA senior service designer seats. Ontario and Saskatchewan buy UX through staffing contracts. Stable, and research-heavy, which suits an HCI master's.

focus_roles.role: Senior product designer, fintech / rules-heavy SaaS
focus_roles.why: Wagepoint, NDAX, Jobber, Visionpool: the reward-engine and tier-system work transfers directly. A safe fallback track that pays well.

deprioritize: Pure graphic/print roles (Job Bank: print demand declining)
Generalist junior UI roles in Toronto (surplus risk, crowded)
AI engineer roles that are engineering-only (low design leverage)

relocation.verdict: Best place to move after graduating
relocation.why: #1 tech-talent growth in North America three years running (+56%, 2022–25), with tech jobs far outpacing local tech graduates. UX pay is on par with Toronto (Robert Half mid ~$102k) at much lower living costs. AI-design employers include Robots & Pencils, Wagepoint and NDAX.

Most new tech jobs and #5 for AI employment, with 60% of Canada's AI jobs in Toronto/Montreal/Vancouver. Junior and generalist UX is saturated, so it pays off only at senior level with an AI or accessibility specialty. Apply remotely first; move only for a strong offer.

relocation.verdict: For the AI network and government service design
relocation.why: Amii, Upper Bound and Government of Alberta service-design hiring. Ranked 42nd overall by CBRE, so job volume is thinner. Visit for Upper Bound in May 2027; move only for a specific role.

relocation.verdict: Stay until graduation, maybe a little longer
relocation.why: Few posts but solid ones (FCC, Cova, Visionpool remote, staffing-agency contracts at $95k mid). Staying is likely worth it if a Saskatchewan-tied pathway matters to you: some routes need Saskatchewan work after graduating. Check this before moving.

items: Rebuild the portfolio around 3 case studies: Journey Engine (enterprise rules → drag-and-drop), MINDS (LLM scaffold for dyslexia, with research method + evaluation), Bookkeeper AI (human-in-the-loop trust).
Ship MINDS as a live, working prototype built with Claude Code. 'I design and build with AI agents' is the line Toronto posts ask for.
Apply now to the Summer 2027 internships (Lyft UX Research, Manulife), if your program allows a summer work term.
Pitch a Mitacs Accelerate project to Orland.
Earn an accessibility credential (IAAP CPACC or WAS) and add a WCAG audit case study.
Submit a thesis paper (e.g., ASSETS/CHI late-breaking) so 'published HCI researcher' is on the CV.
Attend Upper Bound in Edmonton (May 18–21) on a bursary and book 10 coffee chats with Calgary/Edmonton design leads.
Take AI-trainer / design-eval contract hours (DataAnnotation-type) within your allowed hours.
Write one public piece per month on designing AI for neurodivergent users (LinkedIn/Medium).
Get in front of Calgary employers: Platform Calgary events, Co.Labs/UTP in Saskatchewan.
Shortlist 30 target companies (AI-product + accessibility + fintech SaaS) across the 3 regions.
Apply in volume for January 2028 starts; Canadian hiring for new grads and seniors picks up in Q1.
Apply to new-grad cohorts (IBM-type associate programs) and remote-Canada senior roles at the same time.
Negotiate using the Robert Half bands on this page.

apply_now: Robots & Pencils — UX Designer, AI Experiences (Calgary, remote-friendly)
intel.caveats: Rankings come from one seed scan, so treat them as directional until 30+ days of data build up. Job-board snippets can be stale; open the link before applying. This is not immigration or legal advice.
